newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX COB power ends mixed, PV mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX COB power ends mixed, PV mostly higher.

text.p: NYMEX California Oregon Border (COB) electricity futures ended mixed Monday, while Palo Verde (PV) futures moved higher as futures values moved closer to physical power prices, industry sources said.

Next-day Western physical power prices at COB were pegged at $24.00-25.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $24.50-25.50 on Friday, while next-day PV was assessed at $34.00-38.00 from $44.00-46.00 per MWh on Friday.
Although PV physical power prices eased, sources said the numbers remained strong enough to put upward pressure on comparatively lower-valued futures.
June PV futures finished up 38 cents at $26.08 after trade in a range of $25.55-26.15, while July ended up 20 cents at $27.80 after hitting a new contract high of $28.10 and a low of $27.40 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds finished up between 10 and 45 cents, with August and October also trading at new contract highs during the day.
June COB futures settled down 13 cents at $19.40 after trade in a range of $19.00-19.50, while July closed up nine cents at $20.09 from trade in a range of $19.50-20.20 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds finished from 15 cents lower to 25 cents higher.
COB physical power prices were feeling some downward pressure from forecasts of below-normal weather, where power loads were expected to be light, the sources said.

In the Pacific Northwest, weather was expected to turn cooler in southwest Canada, Washington and Oregon over the next two days. Showers were expected through the early part of the week. The coolest temperatures were expected on Wednesday at four to six degrees below normal.
In the Southwest, although PV spot prices eased, they remained at fairly high levels, giving some support to futures, the sources said.
Temperatures in Arizona were expected to hit the high 90s degrees Fahrenheit, with expectations of some continued air-conditioning demand.

Weather in the Southwest was forecast to be three to six degrees above normal in the southern California deserts over the next several days, while thunderstorms were expected in the Arizona and New Mexico mountains keeping temperatures two to four degrees below normal.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 285 COB contracts and 640 PV contracts exchanged hands Monday.
Also, COB open interest for May 16 rose 40 to 5,952, while PV open interest rose 154 to 6,874, NYMEX said.
